title: The impact of the 2013 vocational-education reform on skills, dropout and qualification attainment
title_hu: Az általános és szakképzés hatása a készségekre, a lemorzsolódásra és a végzettség megszerzésére — a 2013-as szakképzési reform hatása
summary_en: Hungary's 2013 vocational-education reform restructured the VET system, shortened the curriculum, and tightened the academic-track / VET division. Hermann and Horn use OKM and administrative qualification data to estimate the reform's effects on student skills (measured at the end of compulsory education), dropout rates, and subsequent qualifications obtained. The chapter quantifies the reform's costs and benefits across student types and across regions.
policy_relevance: Direct relevance for Hungarian VET policy (ITM, Köznevelési Államtitkárság, OFI): provides causal evidence on the 2013 reform's outcomes that should feed the next-generation VET-system design. Particularly important for the ongoing debate over the academic-VET track-allocation age and for EU Recovery-Fund-financed VET investments.
